T: Seven hundred years from home, and dinner's still on time.
D: Thrown back to the Middle Ages, Ash has to recover an ancient book to get home, while a castle full of strangers counts on him.
P: Serve the sausage rolls when Ash is dragged into Lord Arthur's castle in chains.
S: small, loud and impossible to stop at one

Heat the oven to 210C and line two trays. Mix 500g pork sausage mince with the grated onion, crushed fennel, sage, breadcrumbs and pepper. Halve each pastry sheet, lay a line of filling along one long edge, roll up and seal with beaten egg. Cut into 4cm lengths, brush with egg, sprinkle with sesame seeds and snip a small slash in each top. Bake until puffed, golden and cooked through. Serve warm with the tomato relish.
a whole army of them, rattling out of the oven

Heat the oven to 220C and line two trays. On a lightly floured bench, divide the dough into 12, roll each into a 20cm rope and tie a loose knot at each end so it looks like a bone. Lay on the trays and leave to rise a little. Mix the butter, garlic and parsley and brush half over the bones. Bake until golden. Brush with the rest of the garlic butter and sprinkle with the salt and parmesan.
M: carried into the great hall on a board for the whole court

Heat the oven to 200C. Pat the chicken dry, rub with the butter, thyme, salt and pepper and push the lemon halves inside. Toss the carrots, parsnips, onions and garlic with the oil in a roasting tin and sit the chicken on top. Roast for 1 hour. Brush the chicken with the honey and roast until the juices run clear. Rest the chicken on a board and keep the vegetables warm. Stir the flour into the pan juices, whisk in 300ml chicken stock and simmer to a gravy. Carve and serve with the vegetables and gravy.
Great hall roast roots with honey and thyme
Carrots, parsnips and turnips. Shop smart, shop S-Mart
Carrots, parsnips and turnips roasted with honey and thyme until dark at the edges, carried out on the board with the chicken.
W: honey and brown sugar loaf with ginger and cloves, almonds on top, Klaatu barada nikto

Heat the oven to 170C and grease and line a loaf tin. Melt 250g honey with the butter and brown sugar and cool a little. Whisk in the eggs and milk, then fold in the flour, ginger, cinnamon and cloves. Pour into the tin and scatter with the almonds. Bake until a skewer comes out clean. Cool in the tin. Drizzle with the extra honey and serve in thick slices with the cream.
K: Henry the Red's spiced mead punch
mead warmed gently and steeped, served in heavy mugs with orange, for the truce with Arthur
Put everything in a pot and warm gently without letting it boil. Take off the heat and leave to steep. Ladle into 4 heavy mugs with a slice of orange in each.

steps.text: Heat the oven to 200C. Trim the cauliflower, keeping a few inner leaves, and boil whole for 6 minutes, then drain well.
Rub with the butter, thyme, salt and pepper and squeeze over the lemon.
Toss the carrots, parsnips, onions and garlic with the oil in a roasting tin, sit the cauliflower in the middle and roast.
Brush the cauliflower with the honey and roast until deep golden and tender.
Lift the vegetables out, stir the flour into the pan juices, whisk in 300ml vegetable stock and simmer to a gravy.
Cut the cauliflower into wedges and serve with the vegetables and gravy.
